Most evenings start well and drift. You sit down meaning to rest and look up an hour later, more tired than before. This chapter helps you see where your evening goes, then plan one small change.

## Where The Evening Goes

An evening has a shape. There is the stretch straight after work, a middle when energy dips, and the last hour before bed. Each part pulls you in a different direction, so it helps to look at them one at a time.

::: exercise reflection Your Usual Evening
Think about yesterday evening. What did you do in the hour after you got home, and how did you feel at the end of it?

::: lines 6
:::

:::

## Small Changes That Stick

A change sticks when it is small enough to do on a bad day. Pick one thing you can do in five minutes, at the same point each evening, and attach it to something you already do.

::: exercise checklist Before You Start Tonight
Tick each one when it is in place.

- [ ] One five-minute change chosen
- [ ] A cue picked, such as putting the kettle on
- [ ] A note on the fridge to remind you
:::

## Keeping Track Without Fuss

Writing it down for a week shows you what is working. Keep it short: a tick and a word or two is enough.

::: exercise tracker Seven Evenings
Each evening, note whether you made your change and how you felt.

| Evening | Done | How I felt |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | | |
| 2 | | |
| 3 | | |
| 4 | | |
| 5 | | |
| 6 | | |
| 7 | | |
:::

::: exercise fill-in My Evening Plan
Fill in each line.

::: fill-in
My five-minute change is:
I will do it straight after:
If I miss a night, I will:
:::

:::

### Key Takeaways

- An evening has three parts, and each needs its own plan.
- One small change, tied to a cue, lasts longer than a big one.
- A week of notes shows you what to keep.
